recipes.name: 5 Levels of Spaghetti | With Babish
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated shelf stable parmesan, plus more for serving
1 jar cheap tomato sauce (Hunts 15 oz can)
1/2 lb sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
2 slices white sandwich bread, soaked in milk
1 oz freshly grated parmesan, plus more for serving
3 tbsp fresh parsley sprig, finely chopped
3 tbsp fresh basil leaves, finely chopped
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 lb high quality, bronze die spaghetti
freshly grated Grana Padano, for serving
1 1/2 cups ultra premium extra virgin olive oil
3 1/2 lb fresh tomatoes (Red Zebra, cherry, mixed heirloom), blanched and peeled
1 can (14 oz) DOP San Marzano tomatoes
1 lb dry aged Wagyu beef, cubed
2 marrow from beef marrow bones, brined overnight in salt water
1 oz 4 year aged parmesan, finely grated
kosher salt & black pepper (light on salt)
instructions: For Level 1:
For the Lentil Meatball Mixture
Rinse lentils using a fine mesh sieve. - 1 cup dried lentils rinsed
Then, bring a pot of water to boil, adding beef bouillon cubes and stirring until fully dissolved. - 2 ½ cups water - 2 beef bouillon cubes
Add rinsed lentils, cover, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 40 minutes until quite tender but not yet falling apart. - 1 cup dried lentils rinsed

When the lentils are finished cooking, reserve cooking water, strain, then transfer to a rimmed baking sheet to allow them to cool slightly. - For the Lentil Meatball Mixture - 1 ½ tbsp reserved lentil cooking water

Then, transfer the cooled lentils to a mixing bowl, and mash gently using your hands to maintain texture. Add some of the reserved cooking liquid back to the mashed lentils. - 1 ½ tbsp reserved lentil cooking water - 1 cup dried lentils rinsed
For the Panade

In a separate mixing bowl, combine breadcrumbs, milk, whole egg, parmesan, salt, and pepper, dried oregano, and dried parsley. Using a fork, mix to combine, forming a slightly thick panade. - ½ cup Italian style breadcrumbs - ½ cup milk - 1 egg - ¼ cup grated shelf stable parmesan plus more for serving - kosher salt - freshly ground black pepper - ½ tsp dried oregano - ½ tsp dried parsley
For the Lentil Meatballs
Combine the Lentil Meatball Mixture with the Panade and mix by hand until fully incorporated, and meat-like in texture. - Lentil Meatball Mixture - Panade
Roll the mixture into balls, then pan-fry with oil over medium heat until browned. - neutral oil for frying - For the Lentil Meatballs
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a boil for the pasta.
For the Assembly

When the Lentil Meatballs are well-browned, add tomato sauce, and simmer for 10 minutes. Do not simmer for longer than 20 minutes to avoid a metallic taste in the sauce. Add sugar, garlic powder, and onion powder at this time, mixing well with a rubber spatula to incorporate. - 1 jar cheap tomato sauce (Hunts 15 oz can) - 1 tbsp sugar to taste - 1 tsp garlic powder to taste - 1 tsp onion powder to taste - For the Lentil Meatballs
Cook spaghetti al dente according to box instructions. Reserve some pasta cooking water before straining, and return the drained spaghetti to the burner. - 1 lb cheap dried thin spaghetti (Ronzoni)
Add 1 cup of sauce to the cooked spaghetti along with reserved pasta cooking water - cheap tomato sauce (Hunts 15 oz can) - 1 lb cheap dried thin spaghetti (Ronzoni) - ¼ cup pasta cooking water
Toss using tongs, and continue to cook over medium heat for about 1 minute.
Serve hot with 2 meatballs, and finish with shelf-stable parmesan. - grated shelf stable parmesan plus more for serving
For Level 2:
For the Panade
In a medium mixing bowl, combine breadcrumbs and milk to form a thick paste. - ¼ cup Italian breadcrumbs - ¼ cup milk
For the Meatballs

Add beef, egg, cheese, and seasonings. Mix gently by hand. - 1 lb ground beef - 1 egg - ¼ cup shelf stable grated parmesan - ½ tsp garlic powder - ½ tsp dried oregano - ½ tsp dried parsley - ½ tsp onion powder - ¾ tsp kosher salt - ¾ tsp freshly ground pepper
Roll the mixture into meatballs and pan-fry in a fry pan over medium heat until well-browned. - neutral frying oil as needed

Then, add the marinara sauce and simmer for 20 minutes. Transfer to a heat-proof mixing bowl immediately to avoid the metallic taste. Clean the fry pan for the final assembly. - 1 jar marinara sauce (Prego)
For the Assembly
Boil the spaghetti in a high-walled skillet or pot to al dente according to box instructions. - 1 lb spaghetti (Barilla)
Meanwhile, add 1 cup of the sauce back to the nonstick sauce pan over low heat. - marinara sauce (Prego)

Drain the cooked spaghetti, reserving pasta water, and finish cooking in the sauce, tossing with butter, olive oil, and reserved pasta water. Add a pinch of salt and freshly grounded black pepper to taste. - ½ tbsp unsalted butter - drizzle of olive oil - kosher salt - freshly ground pepper
Serve hot, topped with meatballs, and grated parmesan cheese. - shelf stable grated parmesan
For Level 3:
For the Prep
Remove Italian sausage from its casings and set aside the meat in a bowl with the ground beef. - ½ lb sweet Italian sausage casings removed - ½ lb ground beef
Finely chop small white onion and set aside. - ½ small white onion finely minced
Meanwhile, make the panade.
For the Panade

Combine bread and milk into a small mixing bowl and mash into a paste. You can optionally allow the mixture to sit for 10 minutes to ensure total absorption. - 2 slices white sandwich bread soaked in milk

To the panade, add egg, crushed red pepper flakes, crushed garlic cloves, freshly grated parmesan, fresh parsley, fresh basil leaves, season with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper, and dried oregano. Mix to combine. - 1 egg - ½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes - 2 cloves garlic crushed - 1 oz freshly grated parmesan plus more for serving - 3 tbsp fresh parsley sprig finely chopped - 3 tbsp fresh basil leaves finely chopped - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste - ½ tsp dried oregano
For the Meatballs
Combine ground beef, sweet Italian sausage, and Panade until homogenous.
Add the white onion and mix by hand until fully incorporated.
Prepare a small rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper to set individual meatballs on when frying.
Then, shape the mixture into individual meatballs.
Pan-fry over medium heat in oil until well-browned. - neutral oil as needed
For the Assembly
When the meatballs are browned, add the sauce, and simmer for 10 minutes. - 1 jar good quality marinara (Carbone marinara)
Meanwhile, boil spaghetti until al dente. - 1 lb De Cecco spaghetti
Remove the meatballs from the sauce. Then add the spaghetti to the sauce, and toss until coated

Serve hot with a carving fork, topped with meatballs, a little more sauce, freshly grated parmesan, flaky finishing salt, and a couple fresh basil leaves to garnish. Enjoy! - freshly grated parmesan plus more for serving - flaky finishing salt - basil leaves to garnish
For Level 4:
For the Prep
Begin by cutting the chuck roast into 1-inch cubes, and prepare a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. - ½ lb chuck roast
Transfer to the freezer along with the blades of your food processor or meat grinder to chill for about 20 minutes. Alternatively, chill the blades overnight.

Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, reserving one half for the sauce. Then transfer the other half to a frying pan, sautéing over medium heat with neutral oil for around 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant. - ½ white onion finely minced - neutral oil as needed

Add some water to the pan and toss to deglaze before lowering the heat, and adding crushed garlic cloves. Toss to combine and heat through. Remove from heat and allow to cool. Set aside for later use. - water as needed - 2 cloves garlic crushed

Meanwhile, the meat and processor blades should be done in the freezer. Return the blades to the food processor or meat grinder. Add the chilled meat to the food processor. Process and pulse until the meat is pebbly in texture. Set aside while you make the panade
For the Panade
In a mixing bowl, add torn-up pieces of white sandwich bread. Then add buttermilk, mashing the mixture into a thick paste using a rubber spatula. - 2 ½ slices white sandwich bread - ½ cup buttermilk

Make sure the bread is fully saturated before adding the cooled onions and garlic, egg, fresh oregano, basil, and parsley. - 1 egg - 1 tsp oregano finely chopped - 1 tbsp fresh basil finely chopped - 1 tbsp fresh parsley finely chopped

Grate the Grana Padano into the bowl, then add ground nutmeg and ground fennel seeds. Season with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper. - ½ cup freshly grated Grana Padano - ⅛ tsp ground nutmeg - ½ tsp ground fennel seed - kosher salt to taste - freshly ground black pepper to taste
Finally, add anchovy paste, and mix until everything is incorporated. - ½ tbsp anchovy paste
For the Meatballs
Add ground pork and ground veal to the Panade, then add about 1 cup of your home-ground chuck roast. - ½ lb ground pork - ½ lb ground veal - Ground Chuck Roast
Hand-mix until fully incorporated and paste-like.

Meanwhile, add chicken stock to a small mixing bowl and sprinkle a whole packet of powdered gelatin on the surface of the stock. Microwave until the gelatin is completely dissolved (once or twice in short bursts). - ¼ cup chicken stock - 2 tsp powdered gelatin
Then, transfer to a shallow bowl and refrigerate until solid.
Once the gelatin chicken stock has solidified, finely chop, and transfer to the meatball mixture, handmixing until homogenous.
Prepare a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil and a light coating of nonstick cooking spray.
Shape the mixture into evenly sized meatballs and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Broil the meatballs on high for 5-7 minutes, rotating once, until browned on the outside, but not fully cooked through.
For the Sauce
Using an immersion blender, pulse the tomatoes for a few seconds until smooth - 1 can DOP San Marzano tomatoes
In a large sauté pan over medium heat, add olive oil and reserved finely minced white onion. Sweat and sauté 3-5 minutes until soft. - 2 tbsp olive oil - ½ white onion finely minced
Then add crushed garlic and sauté for another 3-5 minutes. - 2 cloves garlic crushed
Add tomato paste, mixing with a wooden spoon to incorporate until the paste begins to stick to the bottom of the pan. - 1 tbsp tomato paste
Then, add the blended tomatoes, scraping up the bottom of the pan, before adding basil stem and parmesan rind. - basil stems - parmesan rind optional
Simmer for about 1 hour on medium heat.
Taste and adjust for seasoning.
For the Assembly
Meanwhile, the meatballs should be finished in the broiler and well-browned. Remove from the oven, and transfer to the sauce.
Simmer the meatballs for about 20 minutes, until cooked through. Keep warm until ready to serve but do not overcook.
Bring a pot of water to boil then cook the bronze-die pasta for 8 minutes. - 1 lb high quality bronze die spaghetti

Ladle finished sauce to a separate stainless steel sauté pan over medium-low heat, then add cooked pasta, pasta cooking water, and olive oil. Toss to coat. - pasta cooking water as needed - olive oil for finishing

Serve immediately with sauce, meatball(s), freshly grated Grana Padano, flaky finishing salt, freshly ground black pepper, a few drops of olive oil, and basil. - freshly grated Grana Padano for serving - flaky finishing salt - freshly ground black pepper - fresh basil julienne
For Level 5:
For the Infused Olive Oil
Preheat the oven to 200°F (95°C).

Combine olive oil, garlic cloves, shallots, bay leaves, peppercorns, and basil in an oven-safe vessel. Cover loosely and place in the oven for 2 hours, allowing flavors to gently infuse without frying. - 1 ½ cups ultra premium extra virgin olive oil - 1 head garlic cloves peeled - 2 shallots roughly chopped - 2 bay leaves - 1 tsp black peppercorns - large handful fresh basil
Remove from the oven, strain, and reserve oil. This oil is used throughout the dish.
For the Sauce

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Using a paring knife, cut a small “X” into the bottom of each fresh tomato. - 3 ½ lb fresh tomatoes (Red Zebra cherry, mixed heirloom), blanched and peeled
Lower tomatoes into boiling water for 30–45 seconds, just until skins begin to split. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking.
Once cool, peel away skins and discard. Roughly chop peeled tomatoes and set aside.
Add garlic cloves and cook for 30–60 seconds, just until fragrant. - 4 garlic cloves finely diced

Add chopped fresh tomatoes, bring to a gentle simmer, then transfer pot to a 225°F (107°C) oven and roast uncovered for 4–6 hours, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes collapse into a thick, dark, jammy paste. - fresh tomatoes (Red Zebra cherry, mixed heirloom), blanched and peeled
Remove from the oven and pass the mixture through a fine mesh sieve to create a smooth tomato paste base.
Return tomato paste to the stove over low heat. Add Bianco DiNapoli tomato sauce. - 1 can Bianco DiNapoli tomato sauce

Heat infused olive oil over low heat. Add finely diced onions and cook very slowly for about 20 minutes, stirring frequently, until onions are deeply softened and jammy but not browned. - Infused Olive Oil (see below) - 2 small onions finely diced
Add garlic and sauté 30 seconds, just until fragrant. - 1 –2 garlic cloves minced
Add the fresh tomato paste base and crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Add basil stems and parmesan rind. - 1 can (14 oz) DOP San Marzano tomatoes - basil stems - parmesan rind
Simmer gently for 30–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, to balance fresh and roasted flavors. Season lightly with salt. Remove basil stems and rind before use. - kosher salt to taste
For the Meat Prep
Cube Wagyu beef, veal, and pancetta. Place on a tray and refrigerate until very cold but not frozen. - 1 lb dry aged Wagyu beef cubed - ½ lb veal chop cubed - ½ lb pancetta diced
Soak marrow bones briefly in salted water if needed. Scoop out marrow, finely chop, and refrigerate. - 2 marrow from beef marrow bones brined overnight in salt water
Chill grinder parts in the freezer for at least 30 minutes. - grinder parts chilled

Grind chilled beef, veal, and pancetta through a coarse grind. Return ground meat to the refrigerator while preparing remaining components. - dry aged Wagyu beef cubed - veal chop cubed - pancetta diced
For the Pesto Binder
In a food processor, combine pine nuts, garlic, currants, and a pinch of salt. Process until very smooth. - head garlic cloves peeled - kosher salt to taste
Add basil leaves and slowly drizzle in infused olive oil while processing until a thick, uniform paste forms. Set aside. - large handful fresh basil - Infused Olive Oil (see below)
For the Panade
Remove crusts from bread, cube, and dry in a low oven if needed. Grind into fine breadcrumbs. - 2 slices white bread crusts removed
In a mixing bowl, combine breadcrumbs and buttermilk until fully hydrated. - buttermilk as needed

Add duck eggs, grated parmesan, porcini powder, fennel seed, nutmeg, MSG, salt, black pepper, and pesto binder. Mix thoroughly until smooth and paste-like. - 2 duck eggs - 1 oz 4 year aged parmesan finely grated - 1 ½ tsp porcini mushroom powder - ½ tsp ground fennel seed - freshly grated nutmeg - MSG to taste - kosher salt & black pepper (light on salt)
For the Meatballs
Transfer ground meat and chopped marrow to a stand mixer fitted with paddle attachment. - marrow from beef marrow bones brined overnight in salt water
Add panade. Mix on low speed until just emulsified and cohesive. Do not overmix.
Shape into large, evenly sized meatballs and set aside.
Heat a saucepan with oil over medium heat. Gently fry meatballs, turning carefully, until evenly browned on all sides. - ultra premium extra virgin olive oil
Transfer meatballs directly into the warm sauce. Bring sauce just to a simmer, then turn off heat. Allow residual heat to finish cooking meatballs gently over 10–15 minutes.
For the Assembly
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook spaghetti until al dente. - luxury artisan spaghetti
Transfer pasta directly into sauce with a splash of pasta water. Finish with butter and gently toss to coat. - butter for finishing

Plate spaghetti into a wide, shallow bowl. Top with a single meatball, extra sauce, finely grated aged parmesan, flaky finishing salt, fresh basil, and a drizzle of infused olive oil. - 4 year aged parmesan for serving - flaky finishing salt - fresh basil julienned - Infused Olive Oil (see below)
Serve immediately.
